speaker: Muse
text: With your current practice budget $100 US / Rs 10,000 India, a $10 IPO bid won’t get you an Indian lot – the minimum bid is around Rs 14,000 and you’d need allotment to even start, so $10 can’t secure entry. On Zerodha delivery for Reliance, brokerage is zero but you still pay about Rs 38.15 on a Rs 10,000 round trip – STT, exchange, SEBI, stamp, GST and a Rs 15.93 DP charge on sale – so you need ~0.38% just to break even before 20% short-term tax if sold within a year. NVDA fractional shares with $100 are easy on a US zero-commission account, but even at a recent ~25% annualised pace you’re looking at ~$125 in a year, not 10x, and spreads are the hidden cost.

speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: CANBK.NS is a textbook risk case: 91% max drawdown in its history means a Rs 10,000 position can become Rs 900 before you blink, and the 23% drop from its high is already flashing that risk. The 29% five-year CAGR looks great until you see revenue falling 9% YoY last quarter while net income flatlined — that's margin compression hiding in plain sight. Beta of 1.25 vs the Nifty amplifies every market downdraft, and with the 10-year at 5.1%, financials face funding cost pressure. For your Rs 10,000 delivery trade on Zerodha, the Rs 15.93 DP charge plus STT means you need 0.38% just to break even before 20% short-term tax — a steep hurdle when the stock's worst day in two years was -6.1%. The 6.9% dividend yield is the only cushion, but it's taxed at slab rates if you're not in the exempt bracket. I'd stay in cash until the October 29th earnings clarify whether the revenue decline is cyclical or structural.
